transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-20 14:30 PST
Duration: 41 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Roberto Singh (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Solstice - Head of Data Protection), Tomás Ruiz (Solstice - Lead Platform Engineer), Priya Nambiar (Solstice - Compliance), Elliot Ward (CTO, joined 14:55)

Auto Summary: quick intake to understand EU residency + HIPAA-like overlap, logging retention requirements and feasibility of Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for our product lines. High level ask: can we prevent full-text logs leaving region and have operator access limited to on-prem or specific cloud region?

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya Chen from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Roberto, our SE. 
[00:18] Roberto: hi all, quick wave. we'll try to run through how Redwood handles region locking, where keys live, and what options you have between our Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments.
[00:35] Lena: thanks. we have a few specific pain points: we do claims processing that sometimes includes health-related notes and also financial identifiers. we need to know where the model inference runs and what logs are kept, and crucially if anything can leave EU jurisdiction.
[00:54] Tomás: and from engineering side, we need to understand operator access, whether root or admin console events are stored, and how audits work — our security team is strict about cross-border ops.
[01:10] Priya: hi, this is Priya, I'll steer compliance. quick context: Solstice is regulated in Ireland and France, we also have small operations in the US but EU data residency is mandatory for EU customers. we also have a binding requirement to not persist raw customer PII/PHI outside region for more than 48 hours.
[01:30] Maya: Great, that's clear. High level — Redwood Hosted gives fastest onboarding but may process in multiple regions unless you enforce regional tenancy. Dedicated gives a reserved GPU pool and can be region-pinned. Private is customer-managed control plane, which can be run in your VPC or on-prem. Each has different operational tradeoffs.
[01:52] Speaker 2: (inaudible) how about keys, where are encryption keys stored?
[01:58] Roberto: KMS integrations — we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. For Hosted we can bring-your-own-key with regional key locations so the keys never leave E U region. For Private, keys are under your remit entirely.
[02:15] Lena: the tricky bit is logs. even if inference occurs in EU, the control plane sometimes needs to surface traces and audit logs that are stored centrally. can those be region-locked?
[02:32] Roberto: yes, so we have per-customer log retention policies and region-locked storage options. Default Hosted keeps traces in our central Cloud but we can offer EU-only log storage for enterprise accounts. However, there are meta traces used for performance dashboards which may be anonymized — we can segregate those.
[02:53] Priya: when you say anonymized, do you redact full user input or do you tokenize? I'm asking because for HIPAA-like PHI we need strict controls, not just masking.
[03:12] Roberto: good question. We have three levels: 1) no retention — drop full payloads at the runtime boundary, 2) redacted retention — we run a deterministic PII/PHI sanitizer and store redacted payloads, 3) full retention for debugging but available only with opt-in and strict contractual S L A. For EU PHI we usually recommend no retention or redacted retention.
[03:35] Tomás: is the sanitizer deterministic? we can't risk inconsistent redaction across datasets — we need repeatable audits.
[03:46] Roberto: yes, deterministic using regex+lookups and context windows. it's not perfect — transcriber note: "k V cash" appeared earlier as mis-parse of KV cache in our docs — but the sanitizer outputs a hash token reference that maps to the audited original if keys held in your KMS.
[04:05] Maya: to add, for Dedicated we can do runtime prefix caching but keep caches in-region and control eviction. For Private on-prem, caches never leave your network.
[04:22] [04:30] Elliot: (joined) Apologies for being late. High level question: can Redwood guarantee that operator (redwood ops) engineers cannot spin up a debugging instance outside EU?
[04:47] Maya: short answer: yes, with Dedicated + explicit regional operator controls and contractual S L A you can restrict operator access. For Hosted there's more guardrails but not zero trust. For Private you control operator scope.
[05:05] Priya: we need to map three use cases: 1) customer-facing claims assistant (PHI heavy), 2) internal transaction scoring (PII + financial id), 3) anonymized analytics. what deployment would you recommend?
[05:23] Roberto: typically claims assistant -> Private or Dedicated with strict region locks and bring-your-own-key. Transaction scoring could be Dedicated if latency and cost are considerations. Analytics could be Hosted with strong anonymization. But we should size workloads to confirm.
[05:43] Tomás: what about backups and audit logs for model versions — they currently store prompts and completions for model debugging. how do we prevent full-text retention?
[05:59] Roberto: we can disable prompt/response persistence, only store token-level metrics and hashes. We also offer a reversible tokenization option where full text is encrypted with your key and stored in EU-only storage; Redwood can't decrypt unless you provide a key (key escrow options discussed later).
[06:20] Lena: key escrow is a red flag — our legal team doesn't like third-party key-hold. we'd prefer KMS with customer-only access.
[06:30] Maya: understood. For Private and Dedicated you can keep keys in your KMS and network, Redwood will never have root key access. For Hosted with BYOK we still sometimes need minimal operator escrow for disaster recovery, but that's negotiable per contract.
[06:48] [07:00] Speaker 2: how do you handle cross-border operator access during incident responses?
[07:10] Roberto: we have strict runbooks: incident response executes in-region by default, but cross-border access can be limited by playbooks requiring customer consent and JIT (just-in-time) admin sessions logged and recorded. We also provide full audit trails (immutable) for those sessions.
[07:31] Priya: audit trails need to be tamper-proof and retained for minimum of seven years — is that feasible?
[07:40] Roberto: yes, we can provide write-once storage for audit trails and configure retention durations; however for Hosted there may be egress fees for long-term storage to your archive.
[07:55] Maya: can I share a quick doc pointer? attached in chat is security-pack.pdf — it details log flows, retention knobs, and KMS patterns.
[08:04] Tomás: saw it. The network diagram mentions a control plane that lives across regions, can you pin the control plane to the EU?
[08:16] Roberto: short answer: with Private yes, control plane is in your VPC. For Dedicated we can run a control plane in-region for enterprise customers. For Hosted it's multi-region for availability but we can provide region-specific tenancy configurations to ensure that sensitive audit data lives in EU buckets only.
[08:35] [09:00] Lena: regulatory question — Schrems II / SCCs: will Redwood act as subprocessors or data controller? we need clarity for our DPA.
[09:14] Maya: Redwood typically acts as a processor. We sign DPA with SCCs where needed, and our legal team supports standard commercial and enterprise DPAs. We also provide export control docs.
[09:29] Priya: and for HIPAA parity — even though HIPAA is US law, we have EU customers with health data; what's your attestation on physical safeguards and encryption for PHI?
[09:44] Roberto: Redwood has a HIPAA-safe configuration. We don't do BAA by default on Hosted — you need enterprise contract. For Dedicated/Private we support BAA and can provide evidence of safeguards (SOC2 type II reports, penetration test summaries).
[09:59] Maya: note: transcript often shows "Redwood Dedicated" as "Redwood Dedicatede" in some automated notes — ignore that typograph.
[10:07] Tomás: ok on RBAC: can roles be scoped to region and to specific teams so EU ops can't see prod logs for US customers?
[10:20] Roberto: yes, RBAC can be scoped by tenant and region; in Dedicated you can create tenant isolation and in Private you can integrate with your SAML/SSO and OIDC providers for fine-grained roles.
[10:36] [11:00] Lena: let's talk retention windows. we mandate that raw inputs be purged within 48 hours unless specifically retained with strong justification. can you support that?
[11:14] Roberto: yes, retention policies are configurable per customer and per route. We support TTL purges at runtime boundary and certified deletion from backups. Caveat: debug snapshots taken by operator for incidents may require special handling — we can require customer approval.
[11:32] Priya: are backups geo-replicated automatically? if so, can we disable cross-region replication for certain datasets?
[11:44] Roberto: absolutely — EU-only buckets and no cross-region replication for sensitive datasets is standard on Dedicated/Private. For Hosted you need an enterprise config to disable replication.
[11:59] Maya: another question from our side — do you plan to allow customers to red-team the redaction process? we find that customers like to test edge-case PHIs.
[12:12] Lena: yes, we'll need to run adversarial prompts to ensure no leakage. That might be part of the pilot.
[12:20] Roberto: we can provide a redaction test harness and evaluation prompts. We'll run privacy-preserving bench tests in a staging cluster pinned to your EU region.
[12:33] [13:00] Tomás: about cost: Dedicated seems expensive, Private more so. do you have guidance on per-inference cost tradeoffs and how batching affects latency for claims workloads?
[13:14] Roberto: batching reduces per-token costs but increases tail latency; for claims assistant you need low tail latency so smaller batches or continuous batching with session-aware routing is ideal. We'll model cost with load profiles during the POC.
[13:36] Priya: what's the acceptable PII/PHI throughput before we need to move to Dedicated? we have spikey loads during month-end claim cycles.
[13:48] Roberto: depends on concurrency and tokens per request, but as a rule of thumb if you need strict operator restrictions and high concurrency with SLOs, Dedicated is advisable. We'll capture numbers in the sizing doc.
[14:05] Maya: quick note — customers sometimes ask about model weights residency: do you require weights to be stored in EU?
[14:14] Lena: yes, for models trained on EU patient data we need weights and fine-tuned checkpoints to stay in-region.
[14:23] Roberto: we support region-locked model caches and image registries. For Private you can host models behind your registry. For Dedicated we can ensure model artifacts live in EU-only storage.
[14:40] [15:00] Priya: any limitations around third-party model providers? e.g., if you pull an open model from an external registry, does that create a cross-border transfer?
[15:12] Roberto: if the model fetch involves a non-EU endpoint, you'd need to mirror the model into an EU registry; we recommend mirroring as part of onboarding.
[15:27] Tomás: okay great. what about logs that contain tokens? some downstream systems index completions for search — we can't have that happen outside EU.
[15:42] Roberto: indexers can be configured to use hashed references or token-level metrics only. Full-text indexing only with your consent and EU-only retention.
[15:55] [16:00] Maya: quick commercial note — Hosted is fastest, Dedicated monthly commit, Private licensing + ops support. We'll propose options after we get your traffic profile.
[16:13] Lena: legal wants to know: will you agree to a clause that prohibits Redwood personnel from accessing raw PHI without two-person approval and customer consent?
[16:27] Maya: yes that's a common enterprise clause. We can add two-person approval and JIT sessions to the contract.
[16:37] Roberto: and all such sessions are audited and write-once stored in EU.
[16:49] [17:00] Speaker 2: noise, background chime, etc
[17:10] Priya: can we talk briefly about on-call access? our policy requires MFA + short-lived credentials for any third-party admin.
[17:22] Roberto: we integrate with your SAML and support ephemeral credentials and JIT access via our identity broker. All events are logged and retained per your retention policy.
[17:40] Tomás: any previous examples of customers with similar constraints?
[17:47] Maya: we've onboarded two EU insurers and a health-tech platform with similar mixes — we can share sanitized case studies and contact references under NDA.
[17:58] Priya: good. next, what about regression monitoring — we need quality monitoring so redactions don't ruin model output quality.
[18:12] Roberto: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to eval prompts, and regression alerts when redaction changes cause hallucinations. We can bind those alerts to your S L A.
[18:28] Lena: that sounds useful. we'll need to see the eval harness.
[18:35] [19:00] Maya: we'll include the eval harness and examples in the package we send.
[19:10] Tomás: last bit — network egress. some of our procurement folks ask for cost predictability if data leaves EU for non-sensitive workloads. how do you instrument egress?
[19:24] Roberto: we provide token-level billing and per-route egress tagging so you can see where egress charges occur. It can be surfaced in Redwood Console and exported to your billing systems.
[19:40] Priya: is there a way to auto-classify routes as sensitive so they always follow EU-only paths?
[19:50] Roberto: yes, route policies can be labeled and policies enforce regional routing and retention.
[20:05] [20:30] Maya: ok, time check — about five minutes left. quick recap and immediate next steps?
[20:36] Lena: recap: we want region-locked processing for claims assistant, BYOK w/ customer-only KMS, 48h raw retention default, redaction test harness, audit trails retained 7+ years, operator JIT sessions with two-person approval.
[20:56] Maya: confirmed. Redwood will send security-pack.pdf, recommended Dedicated vs Private sizing, and a proposal for pilot that includes a redaction test harness.
[21:14] Roberto: I'll own the sizing doc and set up the SE deep dive pilot environment options.
[21:24] Priya: we'll get you the PII/PHI data-flow mapping and retention policy excerpts by next week.
[21:33] Elliot: thanks all, we might do a contract review after the SE deep dive.
[21:39] Maya: great. we'll lock in the deep dive for the week of Jan 4, per earlier note.
[21:46] [22:00] Closing notes: brief cross-talk about calendar invites, someone mis-typed the time zone in the invite earlier (transcript tag: TZ issue), and a final confirmation that Redwood will not ship any demo logs outside of EU for the pilot environment.
